name: Joseph Goebbels
role: Nazi Gauleiter of Berlin and Reich Minister of Propaganda (1933-1945)
summary: Goebbels was a leading Nazi propagandist who, after an early period close to the party's Strasser wing, became a loyal follower of Hitler. His mature positions combine a one-party, leader-centred authoritarian state, extreme racial nationalism and violent antisemitism, hostility to liberalism, democracy and communism, and total mobilisation of society for war. He controlled press, radio, film and the arts and called for a 'people's community' in which class conflict gave way to national duty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 1939 'England's Guilt' article contrasts England's 'social welfare programs' that workers only hear about with German social policy. No statement on health coverage as such.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 1939 he calls capitalist democracy a system suffering from 'every possible modern social ailment' that exploits colonies. He does not defend market allocation as such.

public-ownership.rationale: He calls Germany 'a socialist people's state' (1939 'England's Guilt'). Nationalisation as a programme is not in the texts read, so the answer is low.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1943 Sportpalast speech says 'Rich and poor, high and low must share the burdens equally' in the war effort. This is wartime burden-sharing rather than a tax rate.

unions-good.rationale: Wikipedia reports that trade unions were disbanded in 1933 and replaced by the German Labour Front. He is not recorded arguing for unions' value in the texts read.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said National Socialism sees property among the forces carrying civilisation, in contrast to communism, but also held wartime and racial limits on property (contested).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: 'Don't Be Too Fair!' (1942) says Germans must be taught to hate, and his articles call for hostility toward Jews and enemies. He promoted hatred as propaganda rather than arguing for legal limits on it.

strong-leader.rationale: Wrote that a dictatorship needs a man, an idea and followers and that it may rule against parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: Advocated a dictatorship and total state direction of society, the opposite of a view of the state as harmful.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said no war was lost for having too many soldiers or weapons and demanded all resources for the front.

decide-locally.rationale: Praised the overcoming of provincial peculiarities in 19th-century unification.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: from his demand for draconian and harshest penalties; prisons are not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: 1933 speech: the woman's first and best place is in the family and motherhood; the family is the source of national strength.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: blamed the 'liberal attitude toward the family and the child' for the falling birthrate and promised to reverse it; abortion is not discussed.

more-religion-public.rationale: He invokes God and 'divine providence' in speeches yet attacks churches and clergy. Contested, so 0.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The 1933 'Racial Question' speech says the racial problem will be solved only when the people act 'for their own good', and he rejects redressing wrongs done to Jews. He opposes correcting the position of groups he calls racial enemies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: treated women's maternal 'mission' as natural and warned against the 'masculinization of women'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Presented the regime as guardian of German culture and defended the nation's cultural inheritance against enemies.

gradual-change.rationale: Called himself and the movement revolutionary, and demanded the 'most radical measures'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called for driving foreigners out so Germans can live on German soil (1927, consistent with later racial policy).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Complained that the League of Nations and the 'conscience of the world' may speak about Germany while the German worker may not (1927).

nation-first.rationale: Said what Germany does for its defence is its own business and that it will not tolerate objections; National Socialism is 'for Germans'.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: his 1939 propaganda framed the invasion of Poland as protecting Germans from persecution. Inferred from that framing, and a justification rather than a general statement.

open-borders.rationale: Demanded 'Germany for the Germans' and the removal of foreigners.

revolution-justified.rationale: Wrote that any way of bringing about the revolution was fine and presented the Nazi seizure of power as a revolution.

central-planning.rationale: In 'Total War' (1943) he describes the wartime conversion as following a plan. He never argues that planning beats markets in general.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Described the 1943 plan to close non-essential businesses and reallocate labour and capital to war production.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He drove the mandatory Reich Chamber of Culture (1933), whose sub-chambers controlled entry to each trade, and the Labour Front replaced unions. These are state-organised bodies, though not wage-setting bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended the Nazi single-party state; said parties are outdated and Germany had an authoritarian system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In 'What would there be European about Europe' he praises 'German kaisers and kings, counts and generals' for withstanding attacks from the east. Partial praise of past monarchs, so low.

democracy-best.rationale: Said liberalism and parliamentarianism are outdated, and Germany had replaced democracy with an authoritarian system.

right-to-secede.rationale: Held that unity was won 'through blood and iron' and that no nation may resist the larger order.

natural-rulers.rationale: Said the principle of personality replaced 'popular idiocy' and that propaganda leads the people to the tasks of a 'superior leadership'.

political-violence-never.rationale: Defended a 'merciless war', 'no penalty too severe' against defeatists and extolled Nazi street fighters.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said war drives away dullness and returns people to the sources of their strength, and that Germans had become 'richer, more fulfilled, and better' through it.

separate-church-state.rationale: He attacks churches and clergy and wanted to eliminate the Protestant Church, yet invokes God and divine providence in his speeches. Contested, so 0.

military-superiority.rationale: Called the German army the strongest military force in the world and demanded all resources to defeat rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Demanded 'Germany for the Germans' and celebrated uniting all Germans, defined by blood, in one Reich.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejected Marxism as Jewish and said it destroys the working class; held that struggle is between races and nations.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Called belief in equality 'insane' and championed the principle of personality.

colonial-reparations.rationale: 'The Coffee Drinkers' (1939) and 'England's Guilt' say Britain grows rich by exploiting its colonies. He faults colonial powers for exploitation, though he does not state reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Predicted that in fifty years Europeans would think in continents, and called the war a defence of 'two thousand years of Western civilization'.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned black marketers and shirkers who put selfish interests before the nation's need.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Said each person proves community sense by fulfilling duties before claiming from the community and that women were wrongly given rights at the cost of duties.

limit-population.rationale: Called the declining birthrate a danger of national collapse and said the government would halt it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Said the government was 'everything but reactionary' and a flag-bearer of the future, with a revolution rather than restoration.

means-match-ends.rationale: Said the question is not whether methods are good or bad but whether they succeed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: In 1939 he accuses British capitalists of exploiting colonies and keeping workers in poverty. This attacks capitalist exploitation rather than stating the general claim about profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Condemned Bolshevik rule as terror and class dictatorship.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He blames 'plutocratic' England and the United States for the war, but attributes it to British policy and Jewish interests rather than to capitalism's inner logic.

harm-principle.rationale: In 'More Morality, Less Moralism' (1934) he says the state should regulate the great moral foundations of national life but not the purely personal conduct of individuals. This is only a partial match to a harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Called 'excessive individualism' foreign to National Socialism and put the community first.

conscription.rationale: As Plenipotentiary for Total War he cancelled hundreds of thousands of exemptions to free more men for the front.

media-academia-power.rationale: He describes the press and radio as the 'most influential' instruments for shaping the masses, and says the press creates public opinion. He does not compare these with elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Spoke of fundamental differences between 'two races' and of a Jewish 'nature', but Wikipedia reports he also dismissed 'race-materialism' (contested).

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: The 1933 'Racial Question' speech and 'German Women' say the nation is a community of families and estates rather than of parties and interest groups. Inferred from his rejection of parliamentary parties.

total-state.rationale: As propaganda minister he took control of radio, press, film and the arts; in 1943 he pushed total mobilisation of the economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Said Germany had to be rebuilt on its original foundations after years of decline, calling 1933 a national renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Described the war as about 'living space' and promised a Europe reorganised under German-Italian leadership.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: His Hitler-birthday speeches describe a personal bond between the nation and the Führer, and a 1943 speech says no soldier has broken 'his oath to the Führer'. Authority is tied to personal oaths of loyalty to the leader.

universal-morality.rationale: His 1943 article defends 'the principle of a moral world order' against the enemy, but he applies that morality to the German nation and the Reich. Low, since his morality is national.

single-common-good.rationale: Said parliamentary democracy was a war of interests that wrecked the nation's foundations, in contrast to a unified national will.

workplace-democracy.rationale: In the 1933 'Racial Question' speech he rejects democracy and majority rule and calls parliamentarianism outdated. He says nothing about votes inside companies, so the answer is low.

national-self-determination.rationale: Demanded self-determination for Germans and ethnic Germans, but told the Czechs a nation has no right to resist the larger order (mixed).

force-without-un.rationale: His 1939 and 1941 articles justify the invasions of Poland and the Soviet Union as necessary, with no appeal to any international authority. He endorses force without approval from outside bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Credited 'the power of faith' and healthy instincts, and emphasised emotion and will in propaganda.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: He treats welfare and winter relief as service to 'German people, particularly the working people' rather than to all residents. Inferred from the nationalist framing of social provision.

work-for-welfare.rationale: 'Total War' (1943) says the slackers 'must be shaken out of their comfortable ease' and that everyone who can work must do so during the war. He ties entitlement to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Described National Socialism as uniting farmers, middle class and workers into one people and called for rich and poor to share burdens equally.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Insisted Germany and Italy were the guardians of Europe's cultural heritage and condemned the destruction of museums and artworks.

dominated-front.rationale: Said the 'have-not' young nations want to live and have seen through the rich plutocracies; presented the Axis as such a front.

workers-nation.rationale: Said Marxism was never the idea of a German worker and condemned international communism; called for a 'German worker's state'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said politics and the military belong to men and that women have a different mission, chiefly family and motherhood, while not driving them from work.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Defended the Nazi laws excluding Jews from public life as a legal solution; as minister he pushed Berlin measures such as bans on public transport and marked Jewish shops.

national-mission.rationale: Said National Socialism is 'not for export' (1933) but in 1940-43 claimed a 'European mission' and a new order for Europe (mixed).

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The 1933 'German Women' speech says men must keep politics and the military, which is a claim of male-centred order rather than a rejection of it. Low, since he does not describe patriarchy in these terms.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: His articles call the English and American leaders 'plutocrats' and 'corrupt' and the parliamentary parties 'nonsense' and 'mayflies'. He attacks established political elites as out of touch.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Favoured total state direction of society, culture and economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence on a legal solution to the 'racial problem' and fundamental differences between the races; marriage is not mentioned in the texts read.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Called belief in equality 'insane'; compared Jews to fleas and said all Jews are enemies 'by virtue of birth and race'.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: His articles describe Germany as encircled by 'plutocratic' and Bolshevik enemies and say the Reich must grow stronger to survive. Inferred from that encirclement framing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said a dictator can rule against a parliament but never against the people, yet also that he must bring the nation's will into line with his own (mixed).

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia reports he pressed for the expulsion of Berlin's Jews from 1935 and ordered the yellow badge before the 1941 deportations; his 1941 article endorses the measures.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Described a 'hard century' decided by manliness, hatred and struggle, and war as a source of renewal between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: in the 1933 speeches he calls the parties' 'nonsense' outdated and says the Reich now rests on one movement, and his propaganda attacked Communist parties. Inferred from those statements.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: from his advocacy of dictatorship over parliament and his rejection of parliamentarianism.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: He describes the NSDAP as the party that leads the German people and guides the state. Inferred: he sees a movement leading the nation, though not a working-class vanguard.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: from his view that national unity needs a common 'blood' and that Jews as a distinct race were a destructive force in German life.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: He insists on leadership by the Führer and on the 'personality' of leaders, not chance. Low, since the texts do not address lottery selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Called for 'draconian penalties' and the harshest measures against internal shirkers and defeatists in the national emergency.

party-controls-media.rationale: As minister brought radio, press and film under state and party direction through the Reich Chamber of Culture.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In his 1943 texts he calls for a Europe 'under Axis leadership' rather than a union of equal nations. Low, since he does not mention the EU or pooling as such.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pledged to follow Hitler as Führer in everything; 'Führer command, we follow'.

clerical-rule.rationale: He criticises 'Austrian clericalism' and attacks clergy and churches. He does not endorse religious scholars holding political authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: His articles call on all Germans to support the war effort and attack defeatism, and he treats opposition to the war as betrayal. He opposes working people undermining their own government in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Organised book and art censorship and the Degenerate Art exhibition, but in 1934 opposed a code for purely private conduct (contested).

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: he dismisses parliamentary politics as the 'nonsense' of parties and praises a leader accountable to the nation rather than to voters' parliaments. Inferred from those statements.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He promoted the Axis alliance with Italy and Japan and treats the alliances as the basis of German strength. He does not favour ending military alliances.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: His 1933 'German Women' speech says the German village and countryside are part of the nation's healthy core and that the cities' falling birthrate is the sign of decline. Low, since he does not state the claim in those words.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Celebrated the union of Austria with the Reich: '80 million Germans united'.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: His 1941 'The Jews are Guilty' and 1943 articles mock 'tender sensibilities' of educated people and critics. He treats educated critics as out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Said the Aryan is creative and the Jew destructive, and that Britain and America have hardly any culture of their own beside Germany's.

death-penalty.rationale: Wrote that saboteurs of the war effort deserve the death penalty and that those harming it 'should lose their heads'.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: from his definition of the nation by blood and race.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: 'More Morality, Less Moralism' (1934) mocks moralists who police personal conduct, dress and female behaviour, and argues for private freedom. Only partial support, so low.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: He argues that the press's freedom must find limits where it conflicts with the people and the state, and that the state must guide the economy. Inferred from those statements.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In 1939 he says the state's social principles serve the whole people and attacks rich 'City men' who keep wealth from others. No clear statement on property rights.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Wikipedia reports he backed the 1938 annexation of the Sudeten territory as a return to the Reich. He treated annexations as legitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Publicised trials of clergy and ran propaganda campaigns against the Catholic Church in 1935-37; Wikipedia reports he wanted to eliminate the Protestant church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: He presents Hitler as standing above the parties, 'the Führer', and as the embodiment of the national will. Inferred from that presentation.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Said German unity was established through battles that overcame provincial prejudices and told Czech journalists they could not resist the Reich's order.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He calls the Führer a 'blessed man' with a 'divine gift' for leadership and says history made him leader. Low, since he does not say the ruler is of divine descent.

character-from-environment.rationale: The 1933 'Racial Question' speech and the 1941 articles describe the Jews and others as innately destructive or creative by race, which downplays upbringing as the main cause of character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Wrote that a true dictator depends on himself, not on legal paragraphs, and that hiding behind the law is a sign of weakness.

leader-cult.rationale: Built and promoted the Hitler cult in propaganda and staged mass praise of the Führer.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Celebrated the incorporation of Austria and the Sudetenland and cited persecution of ethnic Germans in Poland.

women-must-cover.rationale: In 1934 he ridicules moralists who would limit women's smoking, bobbed hair and public life, calling such rules out of place in a modern cultural state. He does not address covering clothing directly.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Held that public life and politics should stay a male domain, so equal representation in public bodies runs against his stated view.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: His 1941-1945 articles present German-led Europe as saving the continent from Bolshevism and Jewish-led chaos, and describe Eastern peoples as inferior. Low, since he does not use the term tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said youth must learn respect for sacrifice, duty and the nation; ran a ministry covering youth and culture.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He backed racial exclusion of Jews from public life and treated racial standing as central to national life. Low, since he did not address affirmative action.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: he backed the exclusion of Jews from economic life and the counter-boycott of Jewish shops, which permitted private refusal of service on racial grounds. Inferred from his support for that exclusion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that National Socialism opposes liberalism in theory and practice.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Said Nazis entered parliament to 'shovel out the manure' and that parliamentarianism is outdated.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: 'Total War' (1943) says 'Rich and poor, high and low must share the burdens equally', which casts the privileged as bound to bear their share for the community.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The 1939 'The Coffee Drinkers' article says Germany must cover its needs from its own resources. This is autarky, not a judgment on aid to poor countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Defended the Danzig claim and called Poland's border maps a claim on German territory; attacked Versailles.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: He attacks the anti-Nazi left and calls the opposition to his state a plot of 'Marxist' and 'Jewish' enemies, so he rejects anti-fascism as a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rejected comparisons between Bolshevism and National Socialism as superficial and wrong.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: In the 1933 'Racial Question' speech he quotes Mussolini that Fascism 'is not for export' and says National Socialism is 'a completely German phenomenon'. Inferred: political forms belong to a people.

paid-care-work.rationale: In 'Total War' (1943) he asks women with household help whether they need it, and wants women to work in war industry rather than in domestic service. Low, since he does not discuss paid care directly.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: he rejects parliamentary accountability and praises a leader whose authority rests on the nation's will rather than the instructions of electors. Inferred from those statements.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: in the 1933 speeches he treats parliamentary budgeting as one of the 'parliamentary intrigues' the new government ends. Inferred from that rejection.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: 'Total War' (1943) calls beauty shops and fashion salons 'a waste of time during war' and closes luxury outlets. This is a wartime judgment, not a general view of consumption.

corporate-influence.rationale: He attacks 'plutocratic' power in Britain and the United States and says the press serves plutocratic democracy. He does not discuss corporate lobbying in general.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: said the government was determined to halt the falling birthrate and give families with many children particular attention; a financial incentive is not stated.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Said each must follow all laws and regulations to the letter.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Wrote that every Jew is part of an international conspiracy against Germany and that Jewry manipulates both Bolshevism and plutocracy.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Required silence on war matters and condemned listening to the enemy; the regime banned foreign radio.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said that what Germany does against Jewry is its own business and that it will not tolerate objections from others.

defeat-communism.rationale: Said Bolshevism must be defeated, not coexisted with, whatever the means.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rejected the Marxist view of religion as 'opium' and said National Socialism foregrounds belief in God (his public position).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The 1945 'The Creators of the World's Misfortunes' article says 'Capitalism and Bolshevism have the same Jewish roots' and treats capitalist power as a force of domination. He does not regard capitalism as progressive.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Attacked both Bolshevism and 'plutocratic capitalism' as forms of Jewish power and presented National Socialism as a separate path.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In 1941 and 1943 articles he described the 'destruction of the Jewish race in Europe' as being fulfilled, so he did not deny it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said a dictatorship is subjective and takes sides; as minister he purged press and arts, banned listening to foreign radio and asked no penalty be too severe for defeatists.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He says 'the people want to be led' and describes decisions as made by the Führer on the nation's behalf, not by participatory bodies in workplaces and communities.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: he describes the Führer's leadership as a 'divine gift' and invokes the Almighty over the nation's destiny, which implies authority above the people's will. Inferred from those statements.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Demanded maximum military effort and strength and called the army the nation's defence.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said the only choice is between living under Axis protection or in a Bolshevist Europe.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: In 'England's Guilt' (1939) he says 'the press, which serves plutocratic democracy' brands critics of the social order as rascals. He links press control to wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Wrote that a true dictator relies on himself rather than on legal paragraphs.

racial-franchise.rationale: Said only Germans 'who build this state' may speak and listed excluding Jews from government and public life as the gain of 1933.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Composed the text of the decree authorising the Nazi boycott of Jewish businesses on 1 April 1933 and had Jewish shops marked.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The 1939 'England's Guilt' article says British 'lords and City men' are the richest people on earth while the masses are impoverished and the press serves plutocracy. He treats concentrated wealth as a threat to the people.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Condemned Bolshevism for denying religion on principle.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He treats order and security as the state's first duty and calls for 'draconian penalties' in 'Total War' (1943). He does not regard abolishing police and prisons as acceptable.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He rejects sharing power with the Jews and other groups he calls enemies, and his articles describe divided societies as needing a single national leadership.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1933 'German Women' speech says 'the man' must keep his leading role in life and politics, and that the family is for the woman's motherhood. Marriage authority is not discussed directly.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Praised the Hitler Youth and League of German Girls taking over educational duties and demanded discipline and duty of youth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: His articles and 'Total War' justify killing in war and call for the total defeat of enemies. He does not regard killing as never justified.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Turned the death of SA man Horst Wessel into a martyr cult for the Nazi movement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Cast the war as a struggle against 'satanic forces' and Jewry as the 'incarnation of evil'.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 1941 'The Jews are Guilty' article calls for removing Jews from the German community, and the 1943 'The War and the Jews' says Jews organise the enemy's war economy. He wants the economy in the hands of the German majority.

independent-unions.rationale: Wikipedia reports that unions were disbanded in 1933 and replaced by the German Labour Front. He is not recorded defending unions independent of the state.

family-wage.rationale: The 1933 'German Women' speech puts the family at the centre of the nation and gives men the leading role in life and politics. No explicit wage statement.

person-over-state.rationale: Demanded total sacrifice for the nation and treated individuals as serving the community and war effort.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Said man does not live by bread alone and that the war turned Germans to spiritual things; National Socialism puts belief in God and idealism in the foreground.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The 1933 'Racial Question' speech says the Jews and the German nation have distinct racial interests and that the racial problem must be solved for the nation's security. He treats racial groups as having political interests.

racial-pride.rationale: The 1933 'Racial Question' speech says 'no people with any self esteem could tolerate' the condition of Germany and describes the Aryan as a 'creative creature'. He treats racial pride as legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: 'Total War' (1943) presents the attack on the Soviet Union as a necessary answer to a threat, and calls for the 'most radical' measures. He does not confine armed forces to defence.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The 1945 'Creators of the World's Misfortunes' article and the 1943 'Clay Giant' article say Roosevelt and Churchill plan an occupation of Germany that would destroy and exterminate its people. He says foreign powers plot to dismember Germany.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The 1933 'German Women' speech says women have a 'different mission, a different value' from men, centred on motherhood and care. He values women's distinct role without giving them weight in public policy.

arms-reduction.rationale: Demanded 'total war' and the production of ever more weapons.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Called anyone who speaks of capitulation a traitor and demanded 'no penalty too severe' against undermining the front.

sacred-nation.rationale: Spoke of the 'immortality of the nation' and of the Reich as an eternal community for which to give one's life.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He says the 'human nature' of the Jews and of other peoples differs by race and that the Jewish 'parasitic' nature must be removed. He does not regard a shared human nature as a basis for equal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: In 1933 he calls radio 'the most crucial instrument... for influencing the masses' and says the Ministry will use it for its own purposes. He did not favour media free of government control.

workers-own-party.rationale: He drove the one-party state and called the party system outdated (1933). He did not support working people's own independent party.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He cites the 1933 free election that gave Hitler power as legitimating, yet calls parliamentary democracy and majority rule outdated. Contested, so 0.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said the Nazi movement keeps women out of daily politics; politics and the military 'remain' men's, and women gain nothing by gaining the right to be elected at the cost of motherhood.

race-social-construct.rationale: Treated races as real, opposed collectives with fixed traits ('Aryan' versus 'Jewish') and built policy on them.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The 1933 'German Women' speech says the state should rebuild women's family role and does not see equality agencies as necessary. Low, because the texts do not address agencies directly.

simple-living.rationale: 'Total War' (1943) says Germans are 'voluntarily giving up a significant part of our living standard' and closes luxury shops and restaurants. This is wartime austerity, not a general ideal of simple living.

equal-conscription.rationale: Said the military belongs to men; in 1943 he called women to war work, not to arms.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: In 'Total War' he speaks of defending 'their families, women and children, the beautiful and untouched countryside, their cities and villages' and their two-thousand-year culture. He treats the homeland as a sacred bond.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Cited 'terror and persecution of ethnic Germans' in Poland as a cause of war.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Called the party system outdated and said a dictator must bring the nation's will into line with his own.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Said the government 'does not want to stop the pace of the age' yet roots every age in motherhood and blood.

national-resource-control.rationale: In 'The Coffee Drinkers' (1939) he says Germany cannot cover its needs without colonies, so control of raw materials matters to him. No direct statement on foreign control.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Linked nationalism and a 'socialism' of the people's community; demanded a government of national labour.

notes:
Mature (post-1933 and wartime) positions are used; his early Strasserite, anti-capitalist views (1925-26, partly seen in 'We Demand' 1927 and 'The Nazi-Sozi') are not used for economic answers because Wikipedia reports he accepted Hitler's rejection of expropriation. Not read: the novel Michael (1929) and diary editions (no accessible full text found), so views known mainly from the diaries (e.g. private hostility to churches, policy on homosexuals) are left null. Speeches were meant to persuade, so some statements (religion, 'democratic traits') are public positions rather than private beliefs.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 83 answers taken from it, 78 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Changes of view: in 1925-1926 he wrote anti-capitalist and socialist-leaning texts, then aligned fully with Hitler after 1926; the later record is used throughout. Sources for speeches are translations held by the German Propaganda Archive; the Kristallnacht evidence is a secondhand Nuremberg summary of his remarks. The 1920s German original texts and the full diaries were not read. Several answers rest on Wikipedia, a secondary source, and are marked low or medium for that reason. Positions on the Sportpalast speech are taken from the full translated text. Inferred answers are marked low with 'Inferred:' in the rationale.
